text:
jen.prodsec: FYI - quick restore of `stg-db-20260322` failed during decrypt. Error in restore logs: `KMS: permission denied (cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt)`.

omar.sre: staging or prod?

jen.prodsec: staging. Snapshot object `backups/stg-db-20260322.tar.gz` shows `x-goog-meta-cmek` header is empty when fetched via the new uploader endpoint. Trying a direct gsutil copy returns OK and preserves metadata. :thinking_face:

ira-enc: That smells like the uploader process mutated object metadata. Did we deploy the new `uploader-v2` last night? We also ran the RBAC sweep. Could be two independent issues.

sam-ops: I did the RBAC sweep at 01:50Z. Mostly cleaned stale CI service accounts. I avoided keys used by backups but didn't whitelist legacy `backup-legacy@...` - I thought it was unused.

jen.prodsec: restore job runs as `backup-legacy@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. Logs show it attempted decrypt and KMS returned AccessDenied.

log-bot: Alert: 2 failed decrypts for `projects/redwood-ops/locations/global/keyRings/backups/cryptoKeys/obj-key` between 2026-03-22T02:14:32Z and 02:14:34Z. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/encops-restore

omar.sre: Can someone pull KMS audit logs for that key around 01:45-02:00Z? There was a short window earlier where our logging exporter restarted. If RBAC change happened after that it might not be recorded.

ira-enc: Pulling now. Also checking object metadata history from storage retention logs. If uploader-v2 wrote objects with empty cmek header that would explain missing key reference.

sam-ops: Recreated binding for `backup-legacy` on the KMS key as a quick fix:
```bash
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding obj-key \
  --location global --keyring backups \
  --member serviceAccount:backup-legacy@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```

sam-ops: Confirmed restore job retried and completed successfully.

jen.prodsec: Thanks. Two follow-ups: 1) Why did uploader-v2 strip cmek metadata for newly uploaded snapshot copies? 2) Why does the audit log show a 9m gap between 01:42Z and 01:51Z for KMS admin logs?

ira-enc: Early findings: uploader-v2 introduced a metadata sanitization step to remove PII headers; a regex bug matched `x-goog-meta-cmek` and removed it. I have a patch in review to skip known security headers.

omar.sre: For audit gap, the sink VM rotated its logging agent at 01:45Z due to an automatic update. The agent restarted and missed the final flush. Exporter backlog shows a dropped window. Suggest we add a heartbeat metric and an alert for missing audit-export messages >30s.

sam-ops: Also adding a guard to the RBAC-prune playbook: run `gcloud kms keys test-iam-permissions` for all backup principals before removal. Quick command: ```bash
PERM=$(gcloud kms keys test-iam-permissions obj-key --permissions=cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt --format=json)
if [[ $PERM == "[]" ]]; then echo "no decrypt perms"; else echo "has perms"; fi
```

jen.prodsec: Action items: sam to update RBAC-prune checklist and re-run sweep classification (ETA 3h). ira to merge uploader-v2 fix and roll patch to staging (ETA 2h). omar to add audit-export heartbeat alert + investigate agent auto-update policy (ETA EOD). I'll draft a short RCA and link the canary-runbook.

ira-enc: One more tactical mitigation: uploader should tag uploads with `x-goog-meta-original-uploader: uploader-v2` so we can quickly find affected objects. I'll add that in the patch.

sam-ops: Noted. Also backing up all current key bindings to cloud storage before any further RBAC prunes. Command I used: ```bash
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy obj-key --location global --keyring backups --format=json > /tmp/obj-key-policy.json
```

jen.prodsec: Good. Deciding: no company-wide pager for now, only ops owners notified. I'll create ticket SEC-5991 to track.

log-bot: Ticket created: https://redwood.internal/SEC-5991 - "staging restore failure due to uploader metadata strip + RBAC prune"

omar.sre: Nice catch, team. Closing thread once RCA is attached.
